claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the pickup geofence for a single, unbroken run of 240 seconds - from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:15:00 to the last at 17:19:00, when the trip was cancelled. The POL-NS-01 minimum dwell for a LARGE_VENUE pickup is 300 seconds. The shortfall is 60 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is then not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four limbs hold, and limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the fee_schedule minimum, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the driver's arrival tap. That measured dwell is 240 seconds against 300 seconds for this zone class, so limb (c) fails. The point is not marginal: even on the most driver-favourable reading - running the clock from the 'arrived' event at 17:15:20 rather than from the first fix at 17:15:00 - the driver held position for only 220 seconds before cancelling at 17:19:00, still 80 seconds short. Limb (a) (an arrived event) and limb (d) (cancellation code RIDER_NO_SHOW) do not cure a failed limb (c).

The only route by which a short dwell could be rescued is POL-NS-06(i), which permits separate in-geofence intervals to be accumulated - but only where a traffic_advisory covering the pickup road is present and populated with an admissible type. The sole advisory for this pickup, EV-ADVIS-09103-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own limb report records 'advisory_missing' among the reasons limb (i) is unavailable. There is in any event only one in-geofence interval here, so there is nothing to accumulate. The 60 second shortfall stands unremedied and the full refund follows.

I meet the rider's absence head-on because it does not decide anything under the governing clause. The rider track in the GPS artifact places the rider's device roughly 519 m from the pickup pin with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, and the rider sent no message during the waiting window. I do not dispute either fact. But POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability on the waiting period: on a measured shortfall the fee is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present', because the five-minute wait is the consideration the fee was paid for. The rider's absence does not convert a 240 second hold into a compliant 300 second one.

I do not press POL-NS-04, and I say so plainly rather than stretch it. Limb (a) of that clause requires a chat message from the rider that is locating or coordinating, and the chat log for this trip contains only the system arrival notice at 17:15:21 and two driver messages at 17:15:45 and 17:18:40. No rider message exists, so limb (a) fails on the record. The refund does not depend on POL-NS-04, and the rider's case is unaffected by its unavailability.

The single fact that decides this case - the length of the driver's in-geofence dwell - is carried by EV-GPS-09103 at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no admissibility issues, and it is independently corroborated by the trip record's own figures (wait_time_min 3.7 and cancellation at 17:19:00). No artifact relied on here is impaired, so no confidence cap under POL-GEN-02 bites, and no limb of POL-NS-09 is engaged: there is no direct artifact contradiction, the two 90-day counterparty dispute counters are 0, and the anti-farming counters are not tripped. The case is therefore fully decidable and a full refund of the contested SGD 8.00 is available on this record.

The chat log corroborates the GPS arithmetic from an independent direction: the driver's arrival notice is at 17:15:21 and his own message 'I have to cancel now' is at 17:18:40, with the cancellation entered at 17:19:00. That is under four minutes of waiting. The driver terminated the pickup before the five-minute minimum had run, exactly as the shortfall figure shows.

claims.text: The driver's own trace establishes arrival under POL-NS-02: all 25 of his fixes are inside the pickup geofence, at a mean, minimum and maximum distance of 24.01 m from the pin, against an arrival radius of 120 m for this LARGE_VENUE pickup (Plaza Singapura, level 1 ride-hail bay), and the trace shows a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph — he was stationary at the bay, not passing through it. The driver's statement that he was at the marked bay is corroborated by the trace, so the rider's premise that he was never there fails at the first limb of the test.

The 'arrived' marker at 17:15:20 is genuine, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged. Neither trigger of that clause is met: the trace does not place the driver more than 300 m from the pin (he is 24 m from it), and it does not show him travelling at 15 km/h or above (his only distinct speed is 0.0 kph). There is no false-arrival event to record against this driver, and the rider's characterisation of an early-tap cancellation is not made out on the trace.

Limbs (a) and (d) of POL-NS-01 hold on this record: trip_record contains a driver 'arrived' event for the trip at 17:15:20, the trip shows no boarding event and no start, and the driver terminated it at 17:19:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The driver did not travel to the bay and leave; he arrived, held position, and cancelled on the rider's failure to appear.

The rider's own device never reached the pickup: her track holds 11 fixes, of which 0 qualify, at a mean distance of 519.4 m from the pin — more than three times the 150 m rider-presence radius POL-NS-04 sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. Limb (c) of the rider's exoneration clause is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, and no rider-side exoneration is available on this record.

POL-NS-04 cannot rescue the rider on contact grounds either. The chat log carries three messages and not one of them is from the rider; the only locating content is the driver's own 'At the mall ride-hail bay.' Limb (a) requires a rider message that locates or coordinates, and none exists, while trip_record.in_app_calls is empty so there is no call to weigh. With no rider message there is no 120-second silence interval for limb (b) to measure, and the clause simply does not apply.

POL-NS-03 does not open a refund route for the rider here. That clause applies only where the trace shows the driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin — the wrong-face-of-the-building case. This driver was inside the radius, 24 m from the pin, so there is no wrong-entrance inference to draw and neither limb of the fault allocation comes into play.

The SGD 8.00 charged is exactly the figure the fee_schedule resolution rule produces for this trip: the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), the vehicle tier being the dimension that produces it. The fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line therefore reconciles with the schedule and no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect exists; the rider's objection to the size of the 'XL cancellation fee' identifies no mischarge.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming gate is clear on this driver, and only the two fields that clause names may be read for it: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed trips is 0.83%, far below the 0.08 rate. The driver's lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 2 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot be substituted for the trailing-30-day counter. Nothing on this profile disables the clause that pays the driver, and if the fee is upheld his remedy is 80% of it, SGD 6.40 of SGD 8.00.

The driver does not dispute the one number that goes against him. The effective in-geofence dwell is 240 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 17:15:00 to cancellation at 17:19:00, against the 300-second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup — a 60-second shortfall — and the accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable to make it up because the trace shows only one in-geofence interval and EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so there is no populated advisory to permit separate intervals to be summed. The driver asks that the ruling record, on the clean weight-1.0 evidence, that his arrival was real, that he held position at the bay for the full recorded window, and that the rider was never within 150 m of the pin — so no false-arrival referral and no abuse finding should attach to him.

The factual conflict the parties present — rider says 'only a few minutes', the driver says he was at the marked bay and the rider did not appear — resolves in the driver's favour on the timestamps: acceptance at 17:04:00, arrival at 17:15:20 after a record time-to-arrival of 11.3 minutes, and cancellation at 17:19:00 after a recorded wait of 3.7 minutes, all consistent with a driver who completed the trip to the bay and waited there. There is no contradiction between trip_record and gps_trace on arrival, dwell or termination, so no POL-NS-09(b) conflict arises and the case is decidable on the arithmetic.

ruling.explanation: Rider: your dispute succeeds. The driver did arrive, but the chargeable no-show fee requires a continuous in-geofence hold of 300 seconds for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. The GPS trace shows the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:15:00 and cancellation at 17:19:00 — 240 seconds. Even running the clock from the driver's 17:15:20 arrival tap gives only 220 seconds. POL-NS-01(c) therefore fails, and under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is refunded in full. The 300-second minimum is not reduced by the rider being absent or not replying; POL-NS-06 is strict on the waiting period. The accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) does not rescue the fee: there was only one in-geofence interval, and EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, so there is no populated traffic advisory. The SGD 8.00 charge is the correct cancellation-fee amount — the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) — but it is not chargeable on this record and is refunded in full. Driver: your points are accepted in part. EV-GPS-09103 confirms you were stationary inside the 120 m arrival radius, about 24 m from the pin, and the 17:15:20 arrived marker is genuine, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and no false-arrival referral is made. POL-NS-03 does not apply because you were inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius, not outside it. The rider's track shows no qualifying presence inside the 150 m rider-presence radius and the rider sent no locating chat message, so POL-NS-04 does not apply; but rider absence does not restore the fee because the failure is the short dwell. The anti-farming check does not trip, but because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on limb (c), POL-NS-07 driver compensation is not payable. No artifact carrying the deciding dwell is impaired — the GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown all carry weight 1.0 — and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger applies. The case is decidable without escalation. No referrals are produced.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver. The SGD 8.00 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-09103 is refunded in full to the rider.

The dispute is not about whether the driver showed up. He did: the GPS trace places him about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura level-1 ride-hail bay pin, stationary (single distinct speed 0.0 kph) from 17:15:00, well inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. The 17:15:20 arrival marker was therefore genuine, and POL-NS-05 (false arrival) is not engaged — neither trigger (more than 300 m from the pin, or motion at or above 15 kph) is met.

But the fee requires more than arrival. POL-NS-01(c) demands a continuous hold inside the geofence of at least 300 seconds for this zone class, timed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the arrival tap. The driver held from 17:15:00 and cancelled at 17:19:00 — 240 seconds, a 60-second shortfall. Even on the reading most favourable to the driver (clock from the tap at 17:15:20) he held only 220 seconds, still short. Limb (c) fails, so the fee is not chargeable, and under POL-NS-06 the waiting-period fee is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present or responded. The one route that could have rescued a short hold — summing separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i) — is unavailable twice over: the trace shows only a single in-geofence interval, and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) with no payload to permit accumulation. That absent artifact carries no fact; it is citable only for its absence, and asserting an unavailable limb against it does not help either side.

On the facts each side pressed: the rider's device never entered the 150 m rider-presence radius (11 fixes, 0 qualifying, mean ~519 m from the pin) and the rider sent no chat message, so POL-NS-04 affords no rider-side exoneration — but that does not matter, because POL-NS-06 is strict liability on the waiting period and the rider's absence cannot turn a 240-second hold into a compliant 300-second one. Conversely, the driver's arrival was real and he was not fee-farming; his own case conceded the 240-second hold, and the anti-farming gate is clear (no_show_terminations_30d = 1, rate 1/120 = 0.008). No driver compensation is payable in any event, because POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not; POL-NS-06 expressly withholds compensation on a shortfall. POL-NS-03 does not open any route here: that clause governs a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m, and this driver was 24 m from the pin, inside the radius. The SGD 8.00 figure itself is correct — the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), the vehicle tier producing it — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) mischarge; the rider's objection is not to the amount but to the charge, and the charge fails on the dwell.

On weight and escalation: no artifact relied on is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d) (no clock skew, no sampling gap or missing rider track, chat msg_id sequence and count consistent, fare line reconciles with the schedule), so confidence is not capped below the floor. No POL-NS-09 trigger is met: no direct artifact contradiction on arrival, dwell or presence; both 90-day counterparty dispute counters are 0; the anti-farming check is not tripped and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; and the sole evidence for the deciding fact is not impaired. No referral is produced: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because qualifying in-geofence fixes do exist, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming escalation branch is not engaged. A note for the record, as both parties' briefs correctly recognised: the driver's lifetime prior_no_show_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used as a ground; it does not substitute for no_show_terminations_30d.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this dispute turns on one arithmetic question, and the arithmetic is not in dispute.

To the DRIVER: your arrival is not questioned. Your GPS trace puts you 24.01 m from the pin at the Plaza Singapura ride-hail bay, inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, stationary (single distinct speed 0.0 kph) for the whole recorded window, and trip_record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 17:15:20 with cancellation at 17:19:00 on reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. So limbs (a), (b) and (d) of POL-NS-01 all hold, and we accept your points that no false-arrival marker was set (POL-NS-05 is not engaged: you were 24 m from the pin, not over 300 m, and never at or above 15 kph) and that POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance route does not apply to you. But POL-NS-01 requires all four limbs. Limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, measured from your first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from your 'arrived' tap. Your first qualifying fix is 17:15:00 and the trip was cancelled at 17:19:00 — 240 seconds, a 60 second shortfall. Your own submission concedes this figure. The accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) cannot rescue it: the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, so there is nothing to sum, and the only traffic_advisory for this pickup (EV-ADVIS-09103-01) is MISSING — no payload, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so limb (i) is unavailable on its own terms. Because limb (c) fails, POL-NS-01 does not make the fee chargeable, and POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full whether or not the rider was present. We acknowledge your request that the ruling record your arrival as genuine, that you held position, and that the rider was never within 150 m of the pin; that is what the trace shows, and no false-arrival referral or abuse finding attaches to you. It simply does not change the fee outcome.

To the RIDER: you are refunded the full SGD 8.00 that was charged. POL-NS-06 is strict on the waiting period — the five minutes is the consideration the fee was paid for — so the driver's premature cancellation at 240 seconds decides the case even though your own device never came within 150 m of the pin (roughly 519 m away, 0 qualifying fixes) and you sent no message during the waiting window. You did not need POL-NS-04, and it would not have helped: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from you and the chat log contains only the system arrival notice and two driver messages.

On the amount: the fare breakdown's SGD 8.00 cancellation-fee line reconciles exactly with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), the vehicle tier producing the figure. There is no POL-NS-08(d) mischarge, and the whole of that line is refunded.

On driver compensation: none is payable. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full before it pays, and limb (c) does not hold. For completeness, the clause's anti-farming gate is clear on this driver — no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below 4, and 1/120 is 0.83%, below 0.08 — and only those two named fields may be read for that check; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure is context only under POL-GEN-01 and carries no weight here.

On escalation and referrals: none. No artifact relied on is impaired under POL-NS-08 (no clock skew, no trace gap or short sample, the chat msg_id sequence is complete and matches the trip record's count, and the fare reconciles), so the confidence cap is the full weight of EV-GPS-09103; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the counterparty dispute counters are both 0; the anti-farming check does not trip; and no clause produces a referral. The case is fully decidable, which is why it is decided rather than escalated.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the numbers that decide this case, and the outcome follows from them. The driver's GPS trace shows he did reach the pickup and hold position inside the geofence, but for 240 seconds only — from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:15:00 to the cancellation at 17:19:00. The minimum wait for a large-venue pickup such as Plaza Singapura is 300 seconds. That 60-second shortfall is decisive: under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The rider's claim that the driver cancelled after only a few minutes is therefore supported, and the SGD 8.00 charged is refunded. The amount itself was correctly calculated — the greater of the SGD 4.00 large-venue zone fee and the SGD 8.00 RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee — so the fare line reconciles with the fee schedule and no billing-integrity defect exists (POL-NS-08(d)).

The driver's arguments are accepted so far as they go, but they do not change the result. His arrival was genuine — 25 fixes at 24 m from the pin, stationary throughout — so POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) is not engaged, no false-arrival referral is recorded against him, and his request that the ruling say so is granted. He is also right that the rider's device never came within the 150 m rider-presence radius (her qualifying fix count is 0, mean distance about 519 m) and that she sent no locating or coordinating message, so POL-NS-04 does not apply. But POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability on the waiting period: the rider's absence does not convert a 240-second hold into a compliant 300-second one, and the accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable because the trace shows a single in-geofence interval and the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09103-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. No driver compensation is payable on a shortfall — POL-NS-06 gives none — and his anti-farming position under POL-NS-07 is not reached, because compensation only arises where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not. As he correctly noted, his lifetime prior_no_show_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the trailing-30-day counter POL-NS-07 reads.

The record is clean: no clock skew, no trace gap, the chat log is complete against the recorded message count, and the fare reconciles, so no artifact is impaired and no escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 applies. The charge is refunded in full.

ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the pickup geofence for a single, unbroken run of 240 seconds - from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:15:00 to the last at 17:19:00, when the trip was cancelled. The POL-NS-01 minimum dwell for a LARGE_VENUE pickup is 300 seconds. The shortfall is 60 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is then not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four limbs hold, and limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the fee_schedule minimum, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the driver's arrival tap. That measured dwell is 240 seconds against 300 seconds for this zone class, so limb (c) fails. The point is not marginal: even on the most driver-favourable reading - running the clock from the 'arrived' event at 17:15:20 rather than from the first fix at 17:15:00 - the driver held position for only 220 seconds before cancelling at 17:19:00, still 80 seconds short. Limb (a) (an arrived event) and limb (d) (cancellation code RIDER_NO_SHOW) do not cure a failed limb (c).

The only route by which a short dwell could be rescued is POL-NS-06(i), which permits separate in-geofence intervals to be accumulated - but only where a traffic_advisory covering the pickup road is present and populated with an admissible type. The sole advisory for this pickup, EV-ADVIS-09103-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own limb report records 'advisory_missing' among the reasons limb (i) is unavailable. There is in any event only one in-geofence interval here, so there is nothing to accumulate. The 60 second shortfall stands unremedied and the full refund follows.

I meet the rider's absence head-on because it does not decide anything under the governing clause. The rider track in the GPS artifact places the rider's device roughly 519 m from the pickup pin with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius, and the rider sent no message during the waiting window. I do not dispute either fact. But POL-NS-06 is drafted as strict liability on the waiting period: on a measured shortfall the fee is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present', because the five-minute wait is the consideration the fee was paid for. The rider's absence does not convert a 240 second hold into a compliant 300 second one.

I do not press POL-NS-04, and I say so plainly rather than stretch it. Limb (a) of that clause requires a chat message from the rider that is locating or coordinating, and the chat log for this trip contains only the system arrival notice at 17:15:21 and two driver messages at 17:15:45 and 17:18:40. No rider message exists, so limb (a) fails on the record. The refund does not depend on POL-NS-04, and the rider's case is unaffected by its unavailability.

The single fact that decides this case - the length of the driver's in-geofence dwell - is carried by EV-GPS-09103 at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no admissibility issues, and it is independently corroborated by the trip record's own figures (wait_time_min 3.7 and cancellation at 17:19:00). No artifact relied on here is impaired, so no confidence cap under POL-GEN-02 bites, and no limb of POL-NS-09 is engaged: there is no direct artifact contradiction, the two 90-day counterparty dispute counters are 0, and the anti-farming counters are not tripped. The case is therefore fully decidable and a full refund of the contested SGD 8.00 is available on this record.

The chat log corroborates the GPS arithmetic from an independent direction: the driver's arrival notice is at 17:15:21 and his own message 'I have to cancel now' is at 17:18:40, with the cancellation entered at 17:19:00. That is under four minutes of waiting. The driver terminated the pickup before the five-minute minimum had run, exactly as the shortfall figure shows.

The driver's own trace establishes arrival under POL-NS-02: all 25 of his fixes are inside the pickup geofence, at a mean, minimum and maximum distance of 24.01 m from the pin, against an arrival radius of 120 m for this LARGE_VENUE pickup (Plaza Singapura, level 1 ride-hail bay), and the trace shows a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph — he was stationary at the bay, not passing through it. The driver's statement that he was at the marked bay is corroborated by the trace, so the rider's premise that he was never there fails at the first limb of the test.

The 'arrived' marker at 17:15:20 is genuine, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged. Neither trigger of that clause is met: the trace does not place the driver more than 300 m from the pin (he is 24 m from it), and it does not show him travelling at 15 km/h or above (his only distinct speed is 0.0 kph). There is no false-arrival event to record against this driver, and the rider's characterisation of an early-tap cancellation is not made out on the trace.

Limbs (a) and (d) of POL-NS-01 hold on this record: trip_record contains a driver 'arrived' event for the trip at 17:15:20, the trip shows no boarding event and no start, and the driver terminated it at 17:19:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The driver did not travel to the bay and leave; he arrived, held position, and cancelled on the rider's failure to appear.

The rider's own device never reached the pickup: her track holds 11 fixes, of which 0 qualify, at a mean distance of 519.4 m from the pin — more than three times the 150 m rider-presence radius POL-NS-04 sets for a LARGE_VENUE pickup. Limb (c) of the rider's exoneration clause is therefore affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, and no rider-side exoneration is available on this record.

POL-NS-04 cannot rescue the rider on contact grounds either. The chat log carries three messages and not one of them is from the rider; the only locating content is the driver's own 'At the mall ride-hail bay.' Limb (a) requires a rider message that locates or coordinates, and none exists, while trip_record.in_app_calls is empty so there is no call to weigh. With no rider message there is no 120-second silence interval for limb (b) to measure, and the clause simply does not apply.

POL-NS-03 does not open a refund route for the rider here. That clause applies only where the trace shows the driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin — the wrong-face-of-the-building case. This driver was inside the radius, 24 m from the pin, so there is no wrong-entrance inference to draw and neither limb of the fault allocation comes into play.

The SGD 8.00 charged is exactly the figure the fee_schedule resolution rule produces for this trip: the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), the vehicle tier being the dimension that produces it. The fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line therefore reconciles with the schedule and no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect exists; the rider's objection to the size of the 'XL cancellation fee' identifies no mischarge.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming gate is clear on this driver, and only the two fields that clause names may be read for it: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 120 completed trips is 0.83%, far below the 0.08 rate. The driver's lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 2 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot be substituted for the trailing-30-day counter. Nothing on this profile disables the clause that pays the driver, and if the fee is upheld his remedy is 80% of it, SGD 6.40 of SGD 8.00.
